nodes.name: WO3 film preparation
nodes.procedure: Compact WO3 nanoparticle films were grown on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) substrates via drop-casting followed by annealing in air.
nodes.source_text: First, compact WO3 nanoparticle films were grown on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) substrates via drop-casting followed by annealing in air.

nodes.name: WOx electrochemical reduction
nodes.procedure: The WO3 photoanode undergoes electrochemical reduction for 10s in 0.1 M H2SO4 electrolyte at -0.5 V versus RHE to prepare core-shell amorphous/crystalline WOₓ.

nodes.name: Pt-SA/WOx fabrication
nodes.procedure: Pt-SA/WOₓ photoanode was fabricated by immersing WOₓ in 2,2-bipyridine and Pt cations solution followed by annealing under Ar atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/WOx films are composed of compact small crystals with average grain size of 20-50 nm and average thickness of ≈1.3 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images exhibit that Pt-SA/WOx films are composed of compact small crystals with an average grain size of 20-50 nm (Figure 1b) and the average thickness of Pt-SA/WOx films is ≈1.3 μm as the inset shows...

properties.description: Low magnification SEM of Pt-SA/WOx nanoparticles
High magnification cross-sectional SEM showing Pt-SA/WOx film on FTO

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show individual Pt atoms homogeneously distributed in Pt-SA/WOx with no aggregates; atomic resolution confirms Pt atoms dispersed in WO3 lattice; amorphous layer ~1 nm thick at nanoparticle edge; lattice spacings 0.273 nm (-202) and 0.219 nm (222) of monoclinic WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images present the state of the Pt ions on the WO3 grains (Figure 1c,d). Numerous individual brighter dots are observed in Figure 1c, which are attributed to Pt atoms. No Pt aggregates or Pt nanoparticles are observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of W, O, and Pt elements over Pt-SA/WOx nanoparticles confirmed by STEM image and corresponding energy dispersive spectrometer mapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform distribution of W, O, and Pt elements over the Pt-SA/WOx nanoparticles is confirmed by the STEM image and corresponding energy dispersive spectrometer mapping (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt content in Pt-SA/WOx measured to be 0.21 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The content of Pt in Pt-SA/WOx was measured to be 0.21 wt.% by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of Pt-SA/WOx displays WO3 (PDF#43-1035) with no impurity phase; peaks sharper and more intense for WO3 than WO_x and Pt-SA/WOx; left shift of diffraction peaks for WO_x and Pt-SA/WOx indicates lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Pt-SA/WOx displays the presence of WO3 (PDF#43-1035) along with the diffraction peaks from the FTO, and no impurity phase is detected...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f5/2 (76.09 eV) and Pt 4f7/2 (72.56 eV) peaks indicate positively charged Pt SAs in intermediate oxidation state; W 4f peaks shift to lower binding energies in WOx and Pt-SA/WOx with increased W5+ content (36.68/34.32 eV) verifying oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The binding energies of Pt4f5/2 and Pt4f7/2 peaks of Pt-SA/WOx located at 76.09 and 72.56 eV are higher than those of Pt-NP/WOx and lower than those of PtO2... The W 4f peaks of WOx and Pt-SA/WOx shift to lower binding energies and the corresponding relative content of W5+ species is apparently higher than that of WO3...

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR signal at g=2.003 detected for all samples with increased intensity for WO_x and Pt-SA/WOx compared to WO3, proving higher concentration of oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As exhibited in Figure 2c, an EPR signal at g = 2.003 is detected for WO3, WOx, and Pt-SA/WOx, indicating oxygen vacancies are present in all samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized XANES spectra show white line intensity and absorption edge of Pt-SA/WOx between Pt foil and PtO2, indicating Pt oxidation state >0 and <+4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure 2d) exhibit the white line intensity and absorption edge of Pt-SA/WOx located between Pt foil and PtO2...

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed Pt K-edge EXAFS of Pt-SA/WOx shows Pt-O at 1.63 Å (CN=4.2, 2.08 Å) and Pt-O-W at 2.92 Å (CN=2.5, 3.74 Å); no Pt-Pt or Pt-O-Pt scattering confirms atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An obvious peak at 1.63Å in Pt-SA/WOx can be attributed to the first shell of Pt-O scattering... the coordination number (CN) of the Pt atom to oxygen (Pt-O) is 4.2 at 2.08 Å, and the CN of Pt-O-W bonding is 2.5 at 3.74 Å...

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS shows Pt-O and Pt-O-W scattering path signals at [4.9, 1.6] and [11.0, 2.7] for Pt-SA/WOx; no Pt-Pt bond signal detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the PtL2 edge WT χ(k) spectra of Pt-SA/WOx, two prominent scattering path signals located at [χ(k),χ(R)] of [4.9, 1.6] and [11.0, 2.7] are observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/WOx exhibits broadest absorption edge; band-gap energies calculated as 2.54 eV (WO3), 2.58 eV (WOx), 2.60 eV (Pt-SA/WOx).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Figure 4a, the optical absorption edge of WO3 is ≈480 nm and Pt-SA/WOx exhibits the broadest absorption edge...

nodes.characterization_summary: Work functions: WO3 (5.86 eV), WOx (5.60 eV), Pt-SA/WOx (5.54 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The work functions (WFs) of WO3, WOx, and Pt-SA/WOx were calculated to be 5.86, 5.60, and 5.54 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Positive slopes confirm n-type semiconductors; WOx and Pt-SA/WOx show negative shifts in flat band potential and improved carrier densities compared to WO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mott-Schottky curves were collected to evaluate the charge carrier dynamics on as-prepared samples in Figure 4e... The plots of WOx and Pt-SA/WOx reveal negative shifts of the flat band potential (Efb)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/WOx shows smallest charge transfer resistance compared to WO3 and WOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt-SA/WOx photoanode presents the obviously smallest charge transfer resistance in comparison with WO3 and WOx...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/WOx exhibits lowest fluorescence intensity, indicating suppressed charge recombination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As demonstrated in Figure 4g, the Pt-SA/WOx photoanode exhibits the lowest intensity of fluorescence signal...

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl measurements via CV at scan rates 0.015-0.040 V/s show Pt-SA/WOx has larger double-layer capacitance than WO3, indicating higher ECSA from amorphous morphology and Pt sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) plots (Figure 4i) of WO3 and Pt-SA/WOx were investigated through the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measurements and the cyclic voltammetry curves with different scan rates (0.015-0.040 Vs−1)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-SA/WOx shows stronger adsorption of middle hydroxyl (isopropanol) with blue-shifted ν(C-O) band; promotes carbonyl formation during oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be observed that the ν(C-O) band has an obvious blue shift for PtSA/WOx, indicating that Pt-SA/WOx shows stronger adsorption towards the middle hydroxyl of isopropanol than WO3...

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area FFT pattern confirms amorphous/crystalline homojunction in Pt-SA/WOx; bright spots for crystalline WO3, diffuse ring for amorphous state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) pattern (Figure S3, Supporting Information) further proves the amorphous/crystalline homojunction, the bright spots correspond to the crystalline WO3, and the very diffuse diffraction ring confirms the amorphous state.
